links.outcome: Accuracy and safety errors with clean clinician-defined evidence versus closed-book prompting across 34 LLMs
links.effect: Mean accuracy rose from 73.5% to 94.1%; high-risk error fell from 12.0% to 2.6%; contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%; dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.
links.quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

links.outcome: Safety of standard and agentic RAG retrieval grounding versus clean evidence
links.effect: Standard and agentic RAG did not reproduce clean-evidence safety; agentic RAG improved accuracy and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.
links.quote: Standard RAG and agentic RAG did not reproduce this safety profile: agentic RAG improved accuracy over standard RAG and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.

links.outcome: Rate of dangerous overconfidence in LLM answers across deployment conditions
links.effect: Dangerous overconfidence was 8.0% closed-book, falling to 1.6% with clean evidence, and remained elevated under standard and agentic RAG.
links.quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

unlisted_practices: Scaling model size, context length, or inference-time compute to improve clinical LLM safety (max-context prompting and extra compute did not close the safety gap)
Worst-case, question-level analysis of clinically consequential LLM errors

screen.reason: Evaluates safety metrics across various deployment configurations/safeguards including clean evidence grounding, standard RAG, and agentic RAG on a radiology safety benchmark.
